title: Responses compatibility: preserve RNG context and metadata passthrough across streaming + toolcall
author: Asha Patel
description: Summary: Add a compatibility bridge so Responses-style 'seed' and 'determinism' hints are translated to our internal RNG context and propagated end-to-end through streaming frames and tool/function-call handoffs while preserving arbitrary metadata blobs. Motivation: customers using newer Responses API variants expect deterministic seeds and full metadata passthrough when using streaming + tool calls. Previously we dropped seed hints at the streaming reassembly boundary and flattened/mangled nested metadata on tool outputs which caused nondeterminism and lost provenance. What this PR does: (1) Introduces an RNGContext header and in-band chunk attribute (resp_rng_hint) that maps from seed/determinism flags and survives chunk fragmentation/reassembly; (2) Ensures metadata passthrough by stringifying/roundtripping nested attributes when crossing bridge boundaries and by adding a safe-merge strategy for duplicate keys between model and tool outputs; (3) Adds backpressure awareness to tool/function call streaming so a slow tool does not break the client's deterministic reassembly window; (4) Adds an OpenAI-compat shim layer that accepts both legacy --seed and responses.seed, and emits X-Resp-Seed header for downstream components; (5) Adds integration tests and a compatibility doc in docs/openai/responses-compat.md; (6) Leaves a small feature flag (resp_compat_vnext) to flip behavior for canary customers. Rollout plan: feature flag default off, enable for a small percentage, monitor determinism regression dashboards (console -> perf -> rng-drift), follow with a full rollout after 2 business days of no regressions. Backout: revert flag and a single commit that wires the shim. Notes: non-breaking for clients that do not set seed; small perf overhead due to additional frame attributes (~1-3% CPU at 99th in microbench), acceptable tradeoff for deterministic guarantees.

review_comments: Marco Nguyen: Can you explain the safe-merge semantics when the model and tool both set the same nested key? Author: we tiebreak by source priority (tool > model) but preserve original under _merged_src entries; added explanation in docs and explicit tests.

Priya Shah: Streaming attr adds overhead; what's the perf delta? Author: measured ~1-3% CPU at 99th for heavy small-chunk workloads; added benchmarking numbers to perf lab and a flag to disable in constrained deployments.

Liam O'Connor: Slight nit on header naming (X-Resp-Seed vs X-RNG-Hint). Author: kept X-Resp-Seed for user-facing shim and resp_rng_hint for in-band chunk to avoid header collisions; added comments in code.
CI: flaky streaming reassembly test failed first run; rerun passed.
release_notes: Compatibility: Responses-style seed/determinism hints are now preserved across streaming and tool calls and visible via X-Resp-Seed header. Metadata passthrough: nested metadata from tool outputs is preserved and merged safely. Opt-in via feature flag resp_compat_vnext for staged rollout.
